I'm currently dissecting the train examples provided. I've noted the presence of a vertical divider line composed of 5s, splitting the grid into left and right sides. **Investigating Column Mapping**

I'm now zeroing in on the column transformations. I'm seeing a connection between the item's column on the right side of the divider (column 4) in the input and its corresponding column on the left side in the output. For example 2, if an input item is three columns away from the divider on the right, the output item appears two columns away on the left, but only if the item has a single match with one element on the right. Further data confirms my suspicions.


**Examining Side Swaps**

I'm now diving into the implications of the side swaps observed. In certain examples, the left and right halves of the input grid are simply exchanged in the output. I'm trying to decipher when this swap occurs and when it doesn't. A key aspect seems to be the relative positions of elements to the divider. In the training examples, I am observing that positions are being kept relative to the divider line.

**Analyzing Input Structure**

I've been examining the input's layout. It's organized into 6 rows and 21 columns, with a clear divider at column 10, splitting the data into two equal width sides. On the left, columns 0 through 9 are available, while the right spans from columns 11 through 20. I'm currently counting non-zero elements within each row's left-side data. Row 0 has two "4" values.
